witness_rule: Prepared directly from personally viewed original page images. This is an initial independent interpretation, not final learner help or key. Uncertain lexical choices are explicit; subsequent reconciliation must be a separate artifact.

witnesses.boundary: Complete opening paragraph/argument, Se Hǣlend through heofonum. The final single quote closes the embedded gospel saying; the outer Savior speech continues beyond this section.
witnesses.translation: The Savior said to the proud man: ‘Why were you so withholding of my goods, which I gave you? Why did you neglect the gift that I gave you? I now remove you from my bounty, which I bestowed on you; then you will be a beggar in worldly life. Why were you unwilling to consider that I intend to repay every person the good deed that he did to poor people in my name? I shall repay it to him a hundredfold, as it is uttered and said in my gospel: “Whatever you give to one of these least of mine, you always give it to me, and I give you everlasting joy in heaven in return.”’
uncertainties_for_separate_reconciliatio: wlanc may be translated proud or rich according to context; the title gives rich.
selene is provisionally bounty/gift; verify exact lexical sense and whether removal from a given gift is intended.
woruldlīfe is retained literally as worldly life pending lexical/context check; do not import hereafter merely from the judgment setting.
The model English closes the outer quote editorially; the source text does not.

witnesses.boundary: Complete Preface, Ælfred cyning through hē dēð.
witnesses.translation: King Alfred was the translator of this book, and translated it from book-Latin into English, as it is now done. At times he set word by word, at times sense out of sense, as he could explain it most clearly and most intelligibly, given the diverse and manifold worldly occupations that often troubled him both in mind and in body. Those troubles that befell in his days the kingdoms he had received are very difficult for us to count; and yet, when he had learned this book and translated it from Latin into English prose, he afterwards made it into verse, as it is now done. And now he asks, and entreats in God's name, each of those who may wish to read this book to pray for him, and not to blame him if the reader understands it more correctly than Alfred could; because every man must, according to the measure of his understanding and according to his leisure, speak what he speaks and do what he does.
uncertainties_for_separate_reconciliatio: Bōclæden is literally book-Latin; lexical note may explain literary Latin without silently substituting a historical claim.
earfoðrīme refers to being hard to count/enumerate, not merely difficult troubles.
ge on mōde ge on līchaman and ǣgðer ge are one both...and correlation, not three distinct assertions.

witnesses.translation: Lord, almighty God, Maker and Ruler of all creatures, I ask you, by your great mercy, and by the sign of the holy cross, and by Saint Mary's virginity, and by Saint Michael's obedience, and by the love of all your saints and their merits, that you direct me to you better than I have deserved; and guide me to your will and to my soul's need, better than I myself may know; and establish my mind according to your will and for my soul's need; and strengthen me against the devil's temptations; and remove from me filthy lust and every unrighteousness; and shield me against my enemies, visible and invisible; and teach me to do your will, so that I may love you inwardly before all things, with a clean thought and a clean body. For you are my Creator, my Redeemer, my Help, my Comfort, my Trust and my Hope. May praise and glory be to you now and ever for ever, world without any end. Amen.
uncertainties_for_separate_reconciliatio: trēownes provisionally Trust; verify the noun's exact sense in this predicate list.
tō my soul's ðearf is need/benefit; the repeated phrase may be rendered for the good of my soul.
for with the initial petitions is a ground of entreaty, by/for the sake of, not necessarily ordinary causal because of in every phrase.
